quiz.quiz_title: A Bottle of Dew Master Quiz

questions.question: Why did Rama Natha neglect his inherited land at the beginning of the story?

options.A: He wanted to travel across South East Asia.
options.B: He believed in a magic potion that could turn objects into gold.
options.C: His wife Madhumati asked him to sell the property.
options.D: He was afraid of working outdoors in winter.

questions.explanation: Rama Natha spent all his time and money chasing a mythical magic potion that could convert ordinary objects into gold, neglecting his vast fields.

questions.question: What condition did Sage Mahipati lay down for preparing the magic potion?

options.A: Rama Natha had to buy gold coins from the market.
options.B: Rama Natha had to plant banana trees and collect five litres of morning dew with his own hands.
options.C: Madhumati had to chant magic spells for six years.
options.D: Rama Natha had to donate his land to the village temple.

questions.explanation: Sage Mahipati required Rama Natha to personally clear his fields, plant banana trees, and collect 5 litres of winter morning dew from their leaves.

questions.question: While Rama Natha collected dew, his wife Madhumati harvested and sold the __________ at the market to earn gold coins.

options.B: Copper vessels

questions.explanation: Madhumati gathered the harvested bananas from the massive plantation and sold them at the market for a good price.

questions.question: True or False: The morning dew water turned the copper vessel into gold when Sage Mahipati chanted over it.

options.B: False

questions.explanation: Nothing happened when dew was sprinkled on copper because there was no magic potion; real wealth was created by selling the fruit.

questions.question: What primary moral lesson does Rama Natha learn at the end of the folk tale?

options.A: Magic potions require twelve years instead of six.
options.B: Dew collection is the best way to clean copper.
options.C: True wealth comes from hard work and persistent effort, not magical shortcuts.

questions.explanation: Sage Mahipati's strategy proved to Rama Natha that honest labor and productive agriculture create genuine gold.

quiz.quiz_title: The Raven and the Fox Master Quiz

questions.question: Where was Mr. Raven perched at the start of the poem, and what was he holding?

options.A: On a fence, holding a shiny ring.
options.B: Upon a limb, holding a morsel of food in his beak.
options.C: In a nest, holding a small straw.
options.D: On the ground, holding a piece of cheese.

questions.explanation: The opening lines state that Mr. Raven was perched upon a tree limb holding a morsel of food in his beak.

questions.question: How did Reynard the Fox trick the Raven into opening his beak?

options.A: By threatening to cut down the tree.
options.B: By praising his beauty and asking him to sing so he would be crowned King of the Woods.
options.C: By throwing stones at his branch.
options.D: By offering him a larger piece of bread.

questions.explanation: The Fox flattered the Raven's black plumage and claimed that if his voice matched his looks, he would be King of the Woods.

questions.question: True or False: The Raven successfully sang a beautiful song without dropping his food.

options.B: False

questions.explanation: As soon as the Raven opened his beak to sing, his morsel of food dropped into the Fox's waiting mouth.

questions.question: What moral warning does the Fox give to the Raven at the end of the fable?

options.A: Birds should never fly near foxes.
options.B: Flatterers live at the expense of those who listen to them.
options.C: Singing in the morning is bad for health.
options.D: Tree limbs are unsafe for perching.

questions.explanation: The Fox explains that a lesson in avoiding flattery is worth a morsel of food.

quiz.quiz_title: Rama to the Rescue Master Quiz

questions.question: What sound alerted the wife late at night in 'Rama to the Rescue'?

options.A: A dog barking loudly in the yard.
options.B: A thief digging a hole through their outer wall.
options.C: Heavy rain falling on the roof.
options.D: The Kotwal knocking on their front door.

questions.explanation: The wife heard digging noises against the house wall made by an entering thief.

questions.question: Instead of panicking, the wife quietly alerted her husband by saying '__________! Listen!'

options.B: Ssssh

questions.explanation: The wife used the interjection 'Ssssh!' to instruct her husband to remain silent and listen.

questions.question: How did the couple trick the thief into moving to the yard?

options.A: They offered him a hot meal.
options.B: They spoke loudly about hiding a pot of gold coins in a specific yard location.
options.C: They pretended to leave the house empty.
options.D: They threw gold coins out of the window.

questions.explanation: By loudly discussing a fake hidden treasure in the yard, they lured the thief right to where the Kotwal was waiting.

questions.question: True or False: The thief was caught red-handed by the village Kotwal.

options.B: False

questions.explanation: The Kotwal caught the thief red-handed while he was digging up the fake treasure spot.

quiz.quiz_title: The Unlikely Best Friends Master Quiz

questions.question: Why was Gajaraj the royal elephant sad despite enjoying royal luxuries?

options.A: He was given cold food by the mahout.
options.B: He lacked a companion to play with and suffered from loneliness.
options.C: He was kept tied in a dark cave.
options.D: He wanted to leave the kingdom permanently.

questions.explanation: Gajaraj was lonely because he had no true friends to play with, as his caretaker only looked after physical needs.

questions.question: How did Gajaraj react when Buntee the stray dog entered his shed?

options.A: He chased Buntee away with his trunk.
options.B: He generously shared his meal with Buntee.
options.C: He alerted the royal guards immediately.

questions.explanation: Gajaraj welcomed Buntee warmly and shared his food, initiating their friendship.

questions.question: True or False: Gajaraj continued eating normally after Buntee was sold to a farmer.

options.B: False

questions.explanation: Gajaraj was heartsick and refused both food and his daily bath after Buntee was taken away.

questions.question: How did the King solve Gajaraj's illness?

options.B: By appointing a new mahout.
options.C: By ordering Buntee's immediate return to reunite the best friends.
options.D: By sending Gajaraj to the forest.

questions.explanation: Realizing Gajaraj was grieving his lost friend, the King ordered Buntee to be brought back.

questions.question: What primary desire does the speaker express in Jill Wolf's 'A Friend's Prayer'?

options.B: To be a supportive, loyal, and non-judgmental friend.
options.C: To travel around the world alone.

questions.explanation: The poet prays for grace to understand her friends, support their dreams, and accept them unconditionally.

questions.question: The speaker asks for grace to avoid making critical 'judgements from __________'.

options.B: above

questions.explanation: 'Judgements from afar' refers to forming superficial, harsh opinions without understanding someone closely.

questions.question: What does the metaphor 'use my heart to see' signify?

options.A: Using physical eyesight to inspect clothes.
options.B: Understanding friends through emotional empathy, love, and compassion.

questions.explanation: Seeing with the heart means understanding friends through deep emotional perception rather than outward appearances.

questions.question: What bet did Grandfather propose to Mario regarding his boast about popularity?

options.A: A bet of five silver coins.
options.B: A bet over a bowl of fruit chaat regarding real friends.
options.C: A race to the school gates.

questions.explanation: Grandfather bet a bowl of fruit chaat that Mario did not have as many real friends as he claimed.

questions.question: True or False: Mario succeeded on his very first try sitting on the invisible chair.

options.B: False

questions.explanation: Mario missed the seat and fell flat on his back twice while his classmates laughed at him.

questions.question: Why did Mario remain suspended in mid-air on his third attempt?

options.B: Guneet, Asma, and Deepa physically held him up with their hands.

questions.explanation: Three true friends—Guneet, Asma, and Deepa—caught him and held him up so he wouldn't fall.

questions.question: What key truth about friendship did Mario discover through the invisible chair experiment?

options.A: Popularity at school is the most important goal.
options.B: Real friends support you when you struggle, while fair-weather friends merely laugh.
options.C: Invisible chairs should never be taken to school.
options.D: Fruit chaat is bad for health.

questions.explanation: The test separated dozens of laughing, casual peers from three genuinely supportive true friends.

questions.question: What is the scientific Latin name of the Neem tree mentioned in Chapter 7?

options.B: Azadirachta indica

questions.explanation: Azadirachta indica is the botanical Latin name derived from the Persian phrase Azad Darakhte Hindi.

questions.question: Neem tree twigs (datun) are traditionally used in Indian households to maintain __________ health.

options.B: Vision

questions.explanation: Neem twigs have natural antibacterial properties used as traditional datun for cleaning teeth.

questions.question: How do neem extracts assist farmers in agriculture?

options.B: By serving as cost-effective, eco-friendly pesticides that protect crops without damaging soil.
options.C: By making crops grow without water.

questions.explanation: Neem oil and seed powder act as natural pesticides that repel insects while preserving soil fertility.

questions.question: True or False: 'Courtyard' is an example of an open compound word.

options.B: False

questions.explanation: 'Courtyard' is a closed compound word because there is no space between 'court' and 'yard'.

quiz.quiz_title: What a Bird Thought Master Quiz

questions.question: What was the bird's very first home as described in the opening stanza?

options.A: A straw nest in a tall oak tree.
options.B: A small, round, pale-blue eggshell.
options.C: A cage made of golden wires.

questions.explanation: The bird states: 'I lived first in a little house, and lived there very well; I thought the world was small and round, and made of pale-blue shell.'

questions.question: When the bird moved from its nest to the tree branch, it thought the world was made of __________.

options.B: Leaves

questions.explanation: Seeing green leaves all around on the branch, the bird assumed the world was made of leaves.

questions.question: What realization does the bird arrive at when it flies into the vast blue sky?

options.A: That it can rule over all other animals.
options.B: That the true world is vast and a mystery no single creature can fully explain.
options.C: That the eggshell was better than the sky.

questions.explanation: Flying into open air teaches the bird humility, ending with 'how the world is really made, I cannot tell—can you?'

questions.question: What was Prabhat's main rule when choosing which games to play?

options.B: He played strictly games he was sure of winning.
options.C: He played only indoor board games.
options.D: He played sports only in the morning.

questions.explanation: Prabhat was obsessed with winning and avoided games where he might lose or look bad.

questions.question: True or False: Surya was upset and bitter after losing a badminton match to Prabhat.

options.B: False

questions.explanation: Surya smiled cheerfully and remarked 'It was fun!' regardless of whether he won or lost.

questions.question: What specific incident prompted Prabhat's 'change of heart'?

options.B: Watching Surya play basketball poorly without scoring points, yet smiling cheerfully throughout.

questions.explanation: Seeing Surya enjoy playing basketball despite scoring zero made Prabhat realize sports are meant for fun.

questions.question: What is the core message of 'Change of Heart' regarding sportsmanship?

options.A: Scoreboards are the only measure of athletic success.
options.B: Sports are meant for health, effort, and enjoyment; winning is secondary.
options.C: Students should never try new sports.

questions.explanation: True sportsmanship lies in participating wholeheartedly and enjoying the effort rather than fearing defeat.

questions.question: Where do the children gather every evening to play ball in Georgia Heard's poem?

options.B: In a neighbour's field next to a creek.

questions.explanation: The poem describes playing evening ball games in a neighbour's field right next to a creek.

questions.question: The game comes to an end as darkness falls and __________ is declared the winner.

options.B: The Creek

questions.explanation: The poem concludes with 'game's over. Night wins!', personifying darkness as the ultimate victor.

questions.question: Why is the line 'I can't even catch my breath' written in single-word vertical lines?

options.A: The poet ran out of page space.
options.B: It visually mimics the gasping and panting rhythm of a breathless runner.
options.C: It is an error in printing.

questions.explanation: Concrete poetry formats word layout to visually reinforce the physical sensation described.

quiz.quiz_title: Yoga–a Way of Life Master Quiz

questions.question: From which Sanskrit root verb is the word 'Yoga' derived, and what does it mean?

options.B: Root 'veda', meaning 'to know'.

questions.explanation: Yoga comes from 'yuj', which means joining or uniting mind, body, thought, and action.

questions.question: Who systematized ancient yoga philosophy into the 'Yoga Sutras'?

options.B: Sage Patanjali

questions.explanation: Sage Patanjali codified yoga philosophy into the classical Yoga Sutras.

questions.question: True or False: In English grammar, 'Practice' (with -ce) is a verb, while 'Practise' (with -se) is a noun.

options.B: False

questions.explanation: False: 'Practice' (-ce) is a noun, and 'Practise' (-se) is a verb.

questions.question: What digital tool launched by WHO helps individuals practice yoga globally?

options.B: WHO mYoga app

questions.explanation: The WHO mYoga app provides free audio/video instructional guides in multiple languages.

questions.question: Which regional folk art from Uttarakhand is created using rice paste (biswar) over red clay (geru)?

options.B: Aipan Art

questions.explanation: Aipan is the traditional folk art of Uttarakhand drawn on doorsteps and floors using rice paste over geru.

questions.question: What 4,000-year-old metal casting technique is used in Odisha's Dhokra art?

options.B: Lost-wax technique using clay molds and brass scrap

questions.explanation: Dhokra art utilizes the ancient lost-wax casting method with clay, carved wax, and molten brass scrap.

questions.question: Kondapalli toys from Andhra Pradesh are carved from soft local __________ wood.

options.B: Teak

questions.explanation: Artisans use soft, light Ponuku wood joined with tamarind seed paste to carve Kondapalli toys.

questions.question: True or False: Coconut shell craft from Kerala is non-biodegradable and harms the environment.

options.B: False

questions.explanation: Coconut shell craft upcycles natural organic shells into 100% biodegradable, eco-friendly utility items.

questions.question: What simile does Daphne Lister use in the first stanza to describe flying kites?

options.A: Like heavy clouds in a thunderstorm
options.B: Like coloured birds in the wind-whipped sky
options.C: Like bright stars in the dark night
options.D: Like leaves floating on a river

questions.explanation: The opening lines compare flying kites to 'coloured birds in the wind-whipped sky'.

questions.question: The speaker wishes to climb onto a kite's __________ wings to sail high above.

options.B: Paper

questions.explanation: Kites are made of paper frames, so the speaker imagines riding on paper wings.

questions.question: What bird's-eye view does the child imagine enjoying from above?

options.A: Looking at fish inside a deep ocean.
options.B: Looking right down over the green park and town rooftops.

questions.explanation: Sailing high lets the speaker look down over the park and town rooftops.

chapters.title: Ila Sachani: Embroidering Dreams with Her Feet

questions.question: What physical challenge was Ila Sachani born with in Gujarat?

options.B: She was born without the functional use of her hands.

questions.explanation: Ila Sachani was born without functional hands, forcing her to find creative ways to perform tasks.

questions.question: Which traditional style of embroidery did Ila master using her toes?

options.B: Traditional Kathiawar embroidery with mirror work

questions.explanation: Ila mastered Gujarati Kathiawar embroidery, featuring intricate stitches, peacock motifs, and mirror work.

questions.question: True or False: In grammar, 'many' is used with uncountable nouns like milk, while 'much' is used with countable nouns like threads.

options.B: False

questions.explanation: False: 'Many' is used with countable nouns (many threads), and 'much' is used with uncountable nouns (much milk).

questions.question: What main personal achievement did Ila Sachani earn through her embroidery career?

options.A: She opened a textile factory in Delhi.
options.B: She achieved complete financial independence, national recognition, and awards.
options.D: She moved to a foreign country.

questions.explanation: Ila's artwork gained state and national acclaim, proving that determination leads to self-reliance and financial freedom.
